newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate flat at 8.2 pct, demand low.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate flat at 8.2 pct, demand low.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate was flat at 8.2 percent in sluggish trade on Wednesday because of low demand for kuna on Zagreb's money market.
Most interbank borrowing was made at 8.0 percent, with 15-30 day rate going up to 11 from 10 percent.
Settlements totalled 12.9 million kuna, of which only 4.3 million were new loans, against supply of 220 million kuna.
Dealers said the balance on commercial banks' giro accounts had almost doubled since the beginning of August.
But they expected demand to increase after the banks repaid to the National Bank of Croatia some 227 million 20-day funds from an earlier repo deal with dollars and German marks.
"Today's repurchase of foreign exchange and subscription of central bank bills has drained 393 million kuna from giro accounts," dealer Jasenka Blagaic said.
Tuesday's overnight trade totalled 89 million kuna as two banks sought to square their position.
The central bank calculated the kuna midrates slightly weaker at 5.2530 to the dollar and 3.5520 against the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
